reference_sql:
SELECT campaign_id, channel_id, start_date,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY channel_id ORDER BY start_date, campaign_id) AS start_order
FROM campaigns
alternatives:
SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, c.start_date,
       1 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaigns c2
            WHERE c2.channel_id = c.channel_id
              AND (c2.start_date < c.start_date OR (c2.start_date = c.start_date AND c2.campaign_id < c.campaign_id))) AS start_order
FROM campaigns c

SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, c.start_date, COUNT(c2.campaign_id) + 1 AS start_order
FROM campaigns c
LEFT JOIN campaigns c2 ON c2.channel_id = c.channel_id
  AND (c2.start_date < c.start_date OR (c2.start_date = c.start_date AND c2.campaign_id < c.campaign_id))
GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, c.start_date

other_way.sql:
SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, c.start_date,
       1 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaigns c2
            WHERE c2.channel_id = c.channel_id
              AND (c2.start_date < c.start_date OR (c2.start_date = c.start_date AND c2.campaign_id < c.campaign_id))) AS start_order
FROM campaigns c
other_way.tradeoff: Counting the campaigns that come earlier gives the same numbers on any engine, but the tie-break has to be spelled out by hand.
